description: Parks mapped in OpenStreetMap with the tag leisure=park. The OSM wiki (the community's tagging documentation, a secondary description of the data) defines a park as open space for recreation, usually designed and semi-natural with grass, trees and bushes, located within settlements and nearly always open to the public, and says large national or landscape parks should use other tags such as boundary=national_park. Parks are drawn as areas with a name, and footpaths into them should connect to roads for routing; pitches, playgrounds and similar features inside are tagged separately. Taginfo counted 1,302,083 leisure=park objects on 26 September 2026: 1,214,533 ways, 41,052 relations and 46,498 nodes. Coverage: worldwide, with completeness that varies by place. Access: free download of the planet file or regional extracts. Licence: ODbL 1.0. Caveats: tagging differs between communities, some parks are nodes, and fencing or opening hours are not always recorded. Simulation uses: green space inventories for heat, flood retention, access and emergency gathering place analyses. Related records: OS Open Greenspace, ParkServe and the SDG 11.7.1 urban public space data.
